sources.title: Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56
sources.institution: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
sources.citation: Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. Rome: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. ISBN 92-5-104219-5. https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm
sections_read: Chapter 6, Table 11: lengths of crop development stages
Chapter 6, Table 12: single crop coefficients and mean maximum plant heights, with footnotes
Chapter 7, Table 19: typical soil water characteristics for different soil types
Chapter 8, Table 22: maximum effective rooting depth and soil water depletion fraction
Chapter 8, Table 23: salt tolerance of crops, with its rating key
Chapter 8, Table 24: seasonal yield response functions
sources.geographic_scope: Global guidance. Table 12 values are for non-stressed, well-managed crops in sub-humid climates. Table 11 rows are examples for the regions the table names.
sources.crop_scope: Many field crops. Rows used here: maize (grain), sorghum (grain), beans (dry) and pulses, green gram and cowpeas.
sources.verification_note: Tables read on 14 Nov 2026 from FAO's HTML edition. Title, authors, year and ISBN taken from its title page.
limitations: FAO states that the HTML edition was produced by optical character recognition. One value used from Table 19 contains a visible scanning error.
Values describe standard conditions: a well-watered, well-managed, disease-free crop. Rain-fed smallholder crops usually differ.
The source says stage lengths 'may vary substantially from region to region' and urges users to obtain local information.
There is no row for pigeon pea. Cowpea and green gram share a single row.

sources.title: Irrigation Water Management: Irrigation Water Needs. Training manual no. 3
sources.institution: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), with the International Institute for Land Reclamation and Improvement
sources.citation: Brouwer, C., & Heibloem, M. (1986). Irrigation Water Management: Irrigation Water Needs. Training manual no. 3. Rome: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. https://www.fao.org/4/s2022e/s2022e00.htm
sections_read: Chapter 3, Table 6: indicative values of the total growing period
Chapter 3, Table 14: indicative values of crop water needs and sensitivity to drought, with its introduction
sources.geographic_scope: Global, indicative. Not specific to any region.
sources.crop_scope: Major field crops. Rows used here: maize (grain), sorghum, bean (dry), and the shared sorghum/millet row.
sources.verification_note: Tables read on 14 Nov 2026 from FAO's HTML edition. Title, authors and year taken from its title page.
limitations: The source says its water-need values 'provide a rough estimate and should only be used if the crop water needs cannot be calculated more accurately'.
Published in 1986; newer varieties may have different growing periods.
Sorghum and millet share one row for water need. There are no rows for cowpea, pigeon pea or mung bean.

sources.title: Conservation Agriculture in practice: Species diversification
sources.institution: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
sources.citation: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. Conservation Agriculture in practice: Species diversification. https://www.fao.org/conservation-agriculture/in-practice/species-diversification/en/ (undated web page, accessed 14 November 2026)
sections_read: Section 'Crop rotation', including 'The effects of crop rotation'
sources.geographic_scope: Global guidance, not specific to any region.
sources.crop_scope: Crops in general. No crop or family is named.
sources.verification_note: Page read on 14 Nov 2026. The page carries no date or author.
limitations: General guidance. It gives no measurements, no references and no conditions under which the effects hold.
Written for conservation agriculture systems, which combine rotation with minimal tillage and soil cover.
Speaks of 'crop-specific' pests and diseases; it says nothing about crops of the same botanical family.

sources.title: Sustainable intensification through rotations with grain legumes in Sub-Saharan Africa: A review
sources.citation: Franke, A. C., van den Brand, G. J., Vanlauwe, B., & Giller, K. E. (2018). Sustainable intensification through rotations with grain legumes in Sub-Saharan Africa: A review. Agriculture, Ecosystems & Environment, 261, 172-185. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.agee.2017.09.029
sources.geographic_scope: Sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review of 44 publications and 199 observations.
sources.crop_scope: Grain legumes (including soybean, groundnut and cowpea) followed by cereals (maize, sorghum, millet).
sources.verification_note: Title, authors, journal, volume, pages and year confirmed against the Crossref record for the DOI. Abstract read from the Europe PMC record (PMC5946712, open access) on 14 Nov 2026. The full text was not read.
limitations: Only the abstract was read. Methods, the individual studies and site-level results were not examined.
The abstract notes that agro-ecological zone and cereal type were confounded.
It reports that variability in the effect is large and not well explained.

sources.title: Legumes for improving maize yields and income in semi-arid Kenya
sources.institution: Published in Agriculture, Ecosystems & Environment (Elsevier); study at the ICRAF research station, Machakos
sources.citation: Rao, M. R., & Mathuva, M. N. (2000). Legumes for improving maize yields and income in semi-arid Kenya. Agriculture, Ecosystems & Environment, 78(2), 123-137. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0167-8809(99)00125-5
sources.geographic_scope: One research station at Machakos, Kenya, November 1989 to February 1996.
sources.crop_scope: Maize, cowpea, pigeon pea, and the tree legume gliricidia.
sources.verification_note: Title, authors, journal, volume, issue, pages and year confirmed against the Crossref record for the DOI. Abstract read from the Europe PMC record (AGRICOLA) on 14 Nov 2026. The full text was not read.
limitations: Only the abstract was read. Soil type, rainfall in each season, varieties and management are unknown to this project.
One station and one seven-year period. The results are not a prediction for other farms or later years.
The trial ended in 1996; varieties and conditions have changed since.
